newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pares losses, industry buys.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pares losses, industry buys.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures ended a quiet session on Monday with pared losses on light trade and industry buying, traders said.
Prices fell sharply in the morning after triggering a few sell-stops to establish the lows for the day.
But they regained some ground in the afternoon, with industry buying on the dips providing the support.

At the close, benchmark November stood $21 lower at $1,483 a tonne. It had gapped $5 down at the open and sank to a low of $1,445, seen as the immediate support, after triggering stop-loss selling mainly at $1,475.
This was the worst close since late January. It also marked a sharp reversal from the blistering six-month rally that peaked in late May when the contract hit a twin peak at $2,700.
The market has lost some 12 percent in the last week alone as robustas have come under pressure from Indonesian-led selling.
But some traders said the market was bottoming out in the immediate term and a rebound to an oversold condition could be on the cards.
New York arabica futures also recovered from early weakness to trade mixed ahead of midsession, buoyed by local short-covering.
The U.S. July green coffee stocks data, released after the close of the New York trading on Friday, was seen as neutral to slightly bearish.

The report showed a 219,000 60-kg bags rise in July against earlier expectations of 50,000 to 150,000 bags. But there was no sharp New York's reaction to the news, suggesting that it was already priced into the market.
Overall volume stood at 4,920 lots, with the bulk was in switches. The Sept/Nov spread was traded at $15-$25.

In other news, Vietnam's next coffee crop was expected to be a big one, with yields of robusta and arabica reaching as much as 350,000 tonnes, according to the head of the Vietnam Coffee Corporation (Vinacafe).
Tran Khai was quoted by the English-language Vietnam News on Saturday as saying the 1997/98 crop would be Vietnam's biggest so far.
